mark_breakdown.desc: Correct statement describing the positive skewness and lack of outliers

subparts.solution: The data is positively skewed. There are no outliers.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: Skewness describes the asymmetry of a distribution; when the tail extends toward higher values, it is positively skewed.
step_by_step: Observe the shape of the data distribution.
Identify that data stretches more to the right, showing positive skew.
Check for any data points lying far beyond the whiskers or main cluster to conclude there are no outliers.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Confusing positively skewed (tail to the right) with negatively skewed (tail to the left).

mark_breakdown.desc: Adding frequencies for 3 or more children and dividing by total frequency

subparts.solution: $\frac{3 + 3 + 1}{24} \times 100\% \approx 29.2\%$ of families have 3 or more children.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: The percentage is calculated as the favorable count divided by the total count multiplied by 100%.
step_by_step: Count the families having 3, 4, or more children: $3 + 3 + 1 = 7$.
Divide by the total number of families, $24$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Forgetting to include all categories that meet the '3 or more' condition.
